newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher on trade switches.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher on trade switches.

text.p: COMEX copper ended higher, picking up steam throughout the session on end-of-the-month spread trading despite a volatile day in zinc.
LME's zinc price fell $300 in one hour before recouping about a third of its losses on continued rumors of massive Chinese short positions being squeezed.

"That made copper look all the more impressive," said William O'Neill, senior futures strategist at Merrill Lynch. "There was good merchant buying supporting the market. We're building a base at these levels."
Copper also found support from strong London-based fund buying in aluminum and nickel, he said.
Active September settled up 1.05 cents at 110.75 cents a lb, while the spot month ended 3.70 cents higher at 116.50 cents.
Floor traders reported heavy spread trading before the expiration of the July spot contract Tuesday. The July-September backwardation closed at 5.85 cents.
"There was a lot of shortcovering in July," one trader said. "July open interest was 1,514 lots. So there was a lot of switches today."
Refering to the synchronized increase in COMEX and LME warehouse stocks, O'Neill said, "The warehouse factor has always been overstated. Demand is quite strong."

At least one physical dealer disagreed. "The London Metal Exchange stocks have doubled within one month," he said. "Some people are attributing it to arbitrage. But if you look only a small portion comes from COMEX."
The LME cash price was trading at as much as 6.50 cents over the COMEX cash price two weeks ago. At that point, copper was making a beeline from the COMEX warehouses to LME warehouses within the U.S.

Since June 19, COMEX warehouse stocks declined 18,552 tonnes, while LME warehouses in the U.S. increased 34,775 tonnes. Total LME stocks have increased 99,050 tonnes to 220,600 tonnes in the same time frame.

"There's been a huge build-up in Europe and Singapore," the merchant said. "That's all excess copper. And if the fundamentals are going to have any say in this market, then I would expect lower prices."

COMEX spot is currently trading at a 8.70-cent premium to the LME cash price, although traders said the arbitrage is an aberration in light of the spike in the COMEX spot price before the expiration of the July contract.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
